summary: An outside fire was reported in a field at Washington Street and Potomac Avenue.
Two vehicles crashed with nobody pinned in, and one of the vehicles left before officers arrived.
Three vehicles were reported doing donuts and tearing up equipment on high-speed rail property north of Highway 46; an air unit relayed the location to deputies on the ground.

A semi with a box trailer burned on northbound Interstate 5 at the Copus Road off-ramp. The trailer was about 75 percent involved and a fuel line was leaking; firefighters started a second engine for water supply and called for environmental health because of the trailer's load.
Firefighters went to a two-story house and found nothing showing; the first engine on scene handled it.
A caller reported two people with machetes taking copper wire from a property.
A vehicle went off the roadway and burned completely in the Dustin Acres area, with a small amount of grass burning alongside it.
Two loud bangs were reported in the area of Grace Street near Jefferson Park Court and a call was broadcast for service.
A trash barrel was burning under a mobile home overhang about three feet from the structure; crews arriving found a smoldering barrel to the front of the property and no threat to the building.
A man called in his own stolen car and followed it after a 2006 Ford Coupe was taken from Jeffrey Street near Waco Avenue; deputies set a perimeter.
A caller said he was being chased by a man with a Taser who was already a suspect in an earlier assault.
A possible drunk driver in a white pickup was reported heading east on Brundage Lane at Mount Vernon Avenue.
An electric vehicle burned fully involved; a second engine was started for water supply and traffic was moved around the scene.
A man described as a possible transient and carrying a large kitchen knife followed a resident through the gate of a Lincoln Street apartment complex and was gone when officers looked.
Someone reported an alarm going off at the community mailboxes on Duck Pond Lane, with a person possibly getting into them.

Deputies searched a storage facility after two people in sweatshirts and masks got in. One of them went over the back wall and was last seen heading southeast toward the railroad tracks, and a perimeter was set south of the line.
A large brush fire was reported in a field north of the railroad tracks and appeared to be spreading toward the property.
A woman was reported slapping a man at a White Lane apartment.
Two men in ski masks were reported hiding beside a motel room door and knocking on it while the caller stayed inside with the door locked.
Officers broadcast information on an assault from about an hour earlier; the suspect vehicle was a gray Jeep Wrangler with custom black rims.
Semi and SUV crash injures driver on Highway 65.
Medical aid provided for traumatic injury near Wilson Avenue Bakersfield.
Single vehicle rollover on dirt road near Valpredo Ave.
Person hit with object at Terrace Way apartment.
Reckless semi reported on Highway 166 near Cuyama.
Vegetation fire of about 10 acres near CA-119.
Garage fire response on Jackson Street.
Cardiac arrest reported near Brimley Avenue.
Assault with injured man at Terrace Way apartment.
Person with traumatic injury near E 6th Street.
Trash can and back house fire on Kentucky Street.
